## A hyper-redundant robot based on variable cross-section design

Jianxiao Zheng1,2, Yutong Wu1, Jinsong Liu1, Jinhua Zhang1, Liming Zhou3,*, Gang Chen4

Abstract A variable-section design for hyper-redundant robots is proposed in this paper. In industrial development, especially

in the aerospace industry, nuclear industry, and medical field, where traditional rigid linkage robots are not sufficiently adapted

to the working environment such as narrow and complex space and high-risk working space, and the stiffness of hyper-redundant

robots with equal cross-section is insufficient. In aim to solve this problem, a hyper-redundant robot using variable cross-section

design method and decoupled motion control method is proposed in this paper. The simulation results show that the variable

section design has good mechanical properties and the trajectory planning meets the requirements. A prototype machine was

manufactured to verify its design. Equipped with a nozzle at the end of the robot and completed disinfection operations, shows

the robot was capable of completing various tasks as a platform. The research results will provide a new theoretical basis for the

design of hyper-redundancy. Keywords Variable cross-section · Hyper-redundant robot · Cable-drive · Motion control · RRT* · Monte Carlo

## 1. Introduction

In narrow spaces and special application scenarios, such

as aircraft air inlet quality inspection [1], confined space

welding [2], nuclear power plants [3] and medical fields [4],

traditional rigid robots are no longer able to meet the

requirements of their working spaces [5]. After the research,

it was found that the hyper-redundancy robot is better at

flexibility but poor in rigidity, so there is an urgent need to

design a variable-section hyper-redundancy robot with good

flexibility, better rigidity, and path planning capability.

Further, a variable truncated bionic robot based on improved

RRT(RRT*) algorithm path planning is proposed.

In the structure of hyper-redundant robots, the universal

joint is used as the connection structure, such as the structure

of the serpentine arm of Qin [6]; in joint design, the

mainstream design is the structure of the upper and lower

discs of the rod support link; fluid-driven methods are used

in drive, such as soft robots, but traditional cable-driven

methods are still used in the design which described in this

paper, considering control accuracy and system complexity;

to obtain better control precision in power, screw motor is

used as power. Further, in related studies of variable cross-

section robotic arms, such as Liu [7], the design of variable

conclusions that its position accuracy is high, and in the

In summary, the high degree of freedom of the hyper-

redundant robots can meet the complex working

environment under special working conditions; compared

with the equal cross-sectional design, there is less research

on the robots with variable cross-sectional design. However,

it can be concluded from the structure of the variable cross-

section hyper-redundant robot arm that the stiffness of the

system will be improved and the accuracy of operation at the

end will also be improved due to the decreasing cross-

sectional area; when bending and grasping the object, it can

better fit the surface of the object. Therefore, it is necessary

to study the bionic hyper-redundant robot with variable

cross-section, and the main contents of this paper are:

variable cross-section design of this hyper-redundant robot,

dynamics relationship, and path planning.

## 2. Bionic variable section hyper-redundant robot configuration analysis

### 2.1 Structure design


<!-- Page 3 -->


2

In aim to solve the problem that the stiffness of traditional

hyper-redundant robots decreases because of the longer the

robot arm section, a variable-section joint design is adopted.

Each joint has a decreasing cross-sectional area, resulting in

the structure with the largest cross-section at the front

connected to the motor and the smallest cross-section at the

end operator. The accuracy of the end joints is ensured by the

above design while guaranteeing the stiffness of the front end.

Based on the basic characteristics of hyper-redundancy

robots [9], the following design is made for the bionic

variable-section elephant trunk robot described in this paper:

2 joints are connected by 1 universal joint, with a total of 10

degrees of freedom in five joints; each joint is controlled by

three cables; each cable is controlled by a screw motor. The

filament motors are used as power sources for a total of 15

motors, and the power sources are integrated at the rear end;

to unify the wiring, the motors are arranged in an array.

The structural design of the wire-driven hyper-redundant

robot is shown in Fig. 1. The motion principle is that each

joint is supported by a screw between the upper and lower 2

discs, and 2 joints are connected by a universal joint.

*Fig. 1 Structural design of a variable cross-section hyper-*

redundant robot

Each joint is linked by using three wire cables, and each

wire cable is connected to a linear motor in the drive box at

the rear end, for a total of 15 cables and 15 linear motor

modules (with a stroke of 250 mm). The joint disc design of

each section is approximately the same, with the joint near

the bottom as the first section, and the cross-sectional area of

each section (from the large section to the small section) is

80-70 mm, 70-60 mm, 60-50 mm, 50-40 mm and 40-30 mm.

The first 80 mm section of the disc is selected as an

explanation of the design, which is shown in Fig. 3.

The array of circular holes numbered 1-5 are the 3 mm

holes for cables through the cable distributed in an array of 6

on the circumference, in order, on the circumference of 65

mm, 55 mm, 45 mm, 35 mm, 25 mm diameter, to control the

corresponding 1-5 joints; No. 6 hole is the M6 threaded hole.

As the first four joints, they are distributed on 27.5 mm, 22.5

mm, 17.5 mm, and 15 mm, respectively; the fifth joint is an

M3 threaded hole, but it is also distributed on a 15 mm

circumference. The threaded hole passes through a screw of

50 mm in length, which serves as a support and connects the

upper and lower joint discs of the same joint. Hole 7 is a

circular hole of 5 mm diameter, reserved for subsequent

studies, where can install nozzle, sensors and other devices.

A tab at one end of the joint disc is designed to fit with the

universal joint. The robot arm is connected to the rear drive

box by the chassis in Fig. 1, and the chassis is bolted to the

drive box.

### 2.3 Analysis of advantages of variable crosssection

The advantages of the variable-section bionic elephant trunk

robot over the equal-section robot are as follows: the

mechanical properties of the cantilever beam are better; the

precision and response speed of the cable control at the end

are better than those of the equal-section robot due to the

smaller diameter of the disc; the variable-section robot can

better fit the grasped object and complete the grasping action

due to the gradual reduction of its section when performing

grasping and other work.

### 2.4 Working Principle

The motion mechanism of the robot discussed in this paper

is driven by wire cable and the universal joint is used as the

design of the rotation shaft. Each joint is connected by a

universal joint and each joint is controlled by three wire


<!-- Page 6 -->


5

cables in two directions of "pitch" and "yaw" [11]. The robot

described in this article has five universal joints, therefore it

has ten degrees of freedom.

The first joint uses the universal joint to move relative to

the base, the second joint uses the universal joint to move

relative to the first joint, and so on until the last joint. The

coordinate transformation is made several times during each

movement and feedback to the stepper motor at the back end.

The motor drives the cable to control the movement of the

front-end robot arm. Fig. 9 shows a prototype of a three joint

prototype equipped with a nozzle that can be used for

disinfection operations.

*Fig. 9 The prototype of variable cross-section robot with a*

nozzle (three joints only)

For the three joint hyper-redundant disinfection robot

developed in this article, further motion testing was

conducted on a real machine for disinfection tasks in

complex spaces. The task scenario is disinfection in a narrow

space when common desks and chairs are stacked in the

laboratory, as shown in Fig. 10. The nozzle installed at the

end of the robotic arm successfully completed the

disinfection work under the action of the rope driven joint,

and the operation process was smooth, demonstrating the

possibility of the robot described in this article as a work

platform carrying different end effectors to perform different

tasks.

## 4. Track planning

Robot path planning is an important part of robot motion

control and a necessary process for a robot to complete from

the starting point to the target point [16]. There are many

methods for trajectory planning of robots, such as artificial

potential field method [17], ant colony algorithm, fuzzy

neural network [18], particle swarm optimization, and fast

expanding random tree method. In this paper, the trajectory

planning of the ten-degree-of-freedom elephant nose robot is

carried out by using the improved fast-expanding random

tree algorithm [19].

*Fig. 19 Algorithm flow chart*

The basic fast expanding random tree (RRT) algorithm

regards the starting point of motion as the root node of the

track, regenerates a random point in the moving area, then

searches for the closest tree node aggregated on the random

number as the parent node, expands the unit step in the

direction of the parent node and the random point to form a

sub-node for the new node to be searched. If there is no

collision with the preset obstacle in this expansion, the

expansion is considered successful and this sub-node is

added to the set of extended random trees. If there is a

collision with a preset obstacle and the responsibility for this

expansion fails, select the node again to generate random

points. Each time a node is successfully generated, it is

determined whether it is in the target area or not. Repeat this

until it reaches the target point.

The trajectory planning strategy selected in this paper is

the improved RRT algorithm (RRT*) [20]. In the improved

algorithm, the process of parent node re-selection and

random tree re-routing is added. The process of parent node

re-selection is to calculate the cost of starting point to a new

node within the circle radius of the defined radius and


<!-- Page 10 -->

centered on the new node after each iteration. If a new

random number path with a lower cost than the current one

occurs, the potential parent node will be taken as the new

parent node, and the path with a higher cost will be deleted

to complete the path replacement. The flow chart of the

algorithm is shown in Fig. 19 above.

After the obstacles are set in the preset space, the path-

finding results are shown in Fig. 20. The sphere represents a

preset obstacle. The red and blue lines indicate a failed

wayfinding. The green line is the final result and the sphere

is the preset obstacle.

It can be seen that the improved RRT* algorithm described

in this paper can well meet the robot routing requirements

described, which has been proven that the RRT * algorithm

can be applied in the path finding of super redundant robots,

providing a foundation for the research of path finding

algorithms in complex spaces.

## 5. Conclusion

A bionic hyper-redundant robot based on variable cross-

section design is proposed to solve the problems of

insufficient rigidity of traditional equal-section hyper-

redundant robots. The structure design, kinematics and path

planning of the robot are studied and the following important

conclusions are obtained:

1. The static characteristics of the robot with variable

cross-section discussed in this paper are calculated, and

the advantages of the variable cross-section hyper-

redundant robot to the traditional robot with equal

cross-section are elaborated.

2. A cable-driven variable cross-section hyper-Redundant

robot design is proposed, which has a large cross-

section at the front and a small cross-section at the end.

This design ensures both the flexibility and stiffness of

the robot The small front section ensures good end

operability. The platform design guarantees great

travers ability in a narrow space and provides a design

basis for subsequent research on kinematics.

3. The kinematics performance of the robot is analyzed by

Monte Carlo, D-H, and other methods, and an

improved RRT algorithm is put forward to be applied

to the path-finding of the variable cross-section hyper-

Redundant robot, which avoids the preset obstacles

very well and provides a theoretical basis for the

follow-up study.

4. As a hyper-redundant robot work platform, this design

can be equipped with a nozzle to complete spraying or

disinfection work, as described in the text, and can also

be equipped with a camera at the end to complete

maintenance and other work, which has broad

application prospects.
